## AppPorts v1.9.1（build 32）更新说明 · [直链下载](https://file.shimoko.com/AppPorts)

### 总结

**让常用的应用和数据继续留在身边，让 Mac 的内盘重新有余地。** AppPorts 1.9.1 先让「哪些数据可以迁移」变得更清楚：应用数据列表默认隐藏不可迁移的系统结构，保留允许迁移的子目录；点击「已链接」「挂载迁移」等状态，就能直接找到对应项目，少在层层目录里摸索。

迁移一份大目录时，等待也应该心里有数。新的进度提示会把准备、复制、校验和收尾讲清楚，让你看见当前正在做什么、多久没有新进展。遇到中断，AppPorts 会依据记录继续处理、恢复原入口，或补上剩余清理；无法确认安全时保留数据并说明原因。升级后，已经迁好的应用和目录仍按原记录使用，无需重新搬一遍。

腾出的空间，也应该真正留给你。重签名前需要保留的官方原包，现在自动放进外盘看得见的 `AppPorts Backups` 文件夹，附上说明，供需要时恢复。迁移只搬数据，签名由你单独决定；确认不再需要的旧备份和副本会自动清理，把内盘留给下一份项目、下一段视频，以及接下来想做的事。

日常使用也更顺手了：应用列表及时反映操作结果，普通外盘应用可以排除重复的 Spotlight 索引，目录详情栏会记住你调整的高度。谢谢每一位把问题和使用场景告诉我的朋友，这些改进都来自具体的使用体验。我希望，腾出空间之后，你也能少操一点心。

### 升级提示

**更新后请打开一次 AppPorts。** 这次更新会在所有 macOS 版本上停用并移除「开机自动重签名」的登录任务：旧脚本先被替换成空操作，再停止相关进程并删除登录项；设置页不再显示这项失效开关，仅在旧任务清理失败时提示重试。此后签名相关操作都在应用内显式进行。

**升级不会要求你重做任何事。** 已经迁移的目录留在原处即可：日常使用、插盘后的「接回」、需要时的「还原」，都按已有记录进行，不用先搬回本地再迁一次。这次更新也不会改动应用签名，之前重签过的应用不必为了升级再签一次。唯一例外是经典模式下用符号链接迁移的容器数据——如果要恢复原始签名，请先把它还原回本地；用 APFS 挂载迁移的目录不受影响，可以直接修复签名。

**只有签名被 AppPorts 替换过的应用才需要恢复。** 在带「签名已替换」标记的应用上使用「修复」或「恢复原始签名」，恢复用的是重签前保存的官方原包，不需要开发者私钥。其他应用不必为了「保险」重签。

**为官方签名应用重签前，请连接外置盘。** 即使应用仍安装在内盘，原包也会保存在外盘；没有可写且空间足够的外盘时，操作会在修改正式应用前停止。内盘应用在操作期间仍需要临时工作空间，恢复时也需要连接保存原包的外盘。

**外置盘断开时，目录显示「外置盘未连接」并保持不可写。** 重新连接后会自动接回，也可以在目录行手动挂载；挂载完成前不要让应用在该目录里新建数据，重要数据请另行备份。

挂载迁移仍然需要**未加密的 APFS 外置盘**和 AppPorts 的**完全磁盘访问权限**，请先把 AppPorts 放入「应用程序」文件夹。其他格式的存储仍可用于普通应用和目录迁移。

### 新功能

**迁移进度显示真实工作阶段** — 数据目录和目录迁移的操作窗口按实际阶段显示：等待其他操作结束、准备、扫描源文件、复制文件、写入磁盘、校验文件、切换本地入口、清理旧副本、自动恢复数据入口，每一步都有一句说明，告诉你当前在做什么。百分比只属于文件复制，并注明「此进度仅表示文件复制」，随后还会校验并完成收尾；扫描、校验和清理改为显示本轮已处理项数、已读取字节和当前文件，同时保留总用时与本阶段用时。

**长时间没有进展时会明确说明** — 15 秒没有收到新的文件进度时，窗口会显示距离上次进展的时间，而不是让计时器空转；复制速率超过 3 秒没有更新就隐藏，避免用过时速率造成误判。窗口只报告已知阶段和最后的实际活动，不承诺预计完成时间。

**排除外盘应用索引** — 应用列表工具栏新增入口，把普通独立应用移入外置盘上的专用应用库（`AppPorts.noindex`），让 Spotlight 不再同时索引本地入口和外盘应用，减少重复的搜索结果。本地入口照常使用，Dock 上的图钉会指向新位置。App Store、iOS 应用和套件目录保留原安装路径，暂不处理，外盘的文档和照片搜索不受影响。面板分「已完成」和「未完成」列出每个应用的状态，确认后点「自动处理」。相关反馈：[#67](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/67)。

### 界面与目录浏览

**在列表里直接看清哪些可以迁移** — 应用数据列表默认隐藏不能迁移的系统目录结构，保留允许迁移的子目录，每行提供适用的「迁移」「挂载迁移」或「还原」等操作。与「显示零字节目录」并列新增「显示锁定目录结构」开关，需要排查时可以打开，悬停锁形图标可查看不能迁移的原因。这个开关只控制展示，不会解除系统目录的保护；已迁移、待恢复、读取异常或存在冲突的项目仍保留在列表中。

**状态统计变成精确筛选** — 点击「已链接」「挂载迁移」「现有软链」等统计，目录列表只显示匹配的行，并保留必要的路径上下文；统计数字仍基于筛选前的完整列表，方便随时切换到其他状态，重复点击或清除筛选即可恢复，切换应用或页签会重置这个选择。

**个人目录链接不再算作应用数据** — 容器里指向桌面、下载、影片、音乐、图片的普通快捷入口，不再混入应用数据列表；AppPorts 不会遍历或统计它们的目标大小，也不提供迁移或还原，避免把个人文件误当成某个应用独占的数据。已有受管记录或需要恢复、排查的项目仍会保留。

**目录归属和大小范围更清楚** — 同名的 `Data` 目录会保留所属容器的路径，方便辨认它来自哪里。大小同时标明范围（本卷大小 / 目标大小），并说明各行独立统计、父目录不等于子行相加、逻辑大小不等于实际磁盘占用。

**信息栏高度会被记住** — 信息栏默认收成紧凑的单行路径，仍然保留复制和 Finder 定位；拖动把手调整后的高度会被记住，之后换回较大的窗口也沿用你的选择。

### 改进

**中断后自动接着完成** — 数据迁移、还原和挂载操作中断后，AppPorts 依据实际卷、目录身份和持久化记录决定继续、恢复原入口还是只补上清理，不需要你在副本之间做判断。新位置已经开始写入时，绝不用旧副本覆盖它；身份或内容无法确认时保留材料，并在「操作尚未全部完成」提示里说明原因，附「重试」入口。

**保留原件的收尾不再需要单独页面** — 校验通过的原件由 AppPorts 自动清理并释放空间，无法证明安全时保留并说明原因，不再要求你进入单独的副本管理页面逐个判断归属。

**应用原件清理按原基线立即重试一次** — 应用本体切换后，如果一次清理观察因短暂变化失败，AppPorts 会用同一份已验证基线立即重新核对一次，而不是马上显示待办；后台随后完成清理时，界面也不会留下过时的失败提示。差异持续存在时仍然保留旧副本。

**数据卷改用系统建卷并显式忽略所有权** — 挂载迁移的专用数据卷使用系统方式创建，并明确以忽略所有权的方式挂载，普通用户可以直接写入，不需要改动整块外置盘的所有权设置。旧记录缺少所有权信息时按同一方式解释；需要严格所有权语义的历史操作仍按原记录处理。

**卸载和还原前先确认本地入口可访问** — 移除挂载或切回本地数据之前，AppPorts 会实际打开并读取本地目录，核对事务、目标目录和写入者；访问被拒绝或租约失败时保留当前挂载，并给出「访问权限设置」和「重试」入口，不会先卸载再发现本地目录不可用。「还原」入口在已挂载、待挂载和外置盘未连接三种状态下都可见，中断的还原会从同一入口接着完成。

**旧迁移可以直接还原** — 即使目录按新版规则不再允许新迁移，已有受管链接仍保留「还原」入口；标记为「待规范」的旧链接也能直接还原，不必先整理到新路径。相关反馈：[#65](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/65)。

**长时间任务不再被固定总时限截断** — 后台挂载任务原先有一个统一的强制退出时限，大目录的复制和校验可能因此半途结束；现在不再对整项操作设固定期限，每条磁盘命令保留自己的期限和错误传播，中断后仍可从普通入口重试。操作进行中退出 AppPorts 时，也会先取消并等待当前操作安全收尾，而不是在写入中途直接结束进程。

**后台挂载任务跟随 AppPorts 更新** — 任务定义开始包含当前程序签名的标识：AppPorts 更新或移动导致签名变化时重新注册，服务缺失时补注册；还原尚未完成期间任务保持安装，最后一项还原和清理完成后才移除。

**签名原包自动保存到外盘** — AppPorts 自动优先使用应用所在外盘，其次使用已有外部应用库所在盘，再选择其他可写且空间足够的外盘。原包放在盘根目录可见的 `AppPorts Backups` 文件夹，附 `README.txt`，不增加位置选择或管理页面；没有可用外盘时先停止操作。应用与原包同卷时直接改名保留，跨卷则复制并验证成功后清理内部暂存。仍有用的旧内部原包会自动迁出；只有来源信息已有独立保留或官方状态已经核实时，才清理失去恢复能力的旧记录。

**签名原包按恢复价值保留和退休** — 重签前保存的官方原包会一直保留，只要它还有恢复价值；只有确认官方状态已经回来（同一开发者的已验证更新或重装，并检查签名、数据和应用组依赖）才会退休。签名哈希变化本身从不作为删除依据，离线、损坏、身份不确定或来源未知的原包一律保留。同一版本连续重签也不会覆盖最初保存的官方原包。恢复原始签名直接从保存的原包进行，不需要开发者私钥。

**一次最终完整校验，元数据按范围核对** — 复制过程中不再重复逐文件读回；在写入并同步、所有进度回调结束之后，对目标做一次完整的内容、元数据和结构校验，源也再次核对，全部通过才切换。校验复用同一次完整扫描，减少大目录的重复读取。来源标记和按应用授权标记由系统维护，不复制、不删除，也不会因为它们变化就判定内容被修改；应用自己的扩展属性、ACL、权限、资源叉和内容仍按原要求核对。

**只有真正在写入的进程会阻止操作** — 判断写入者时按每个文件描述符的访问方式区分：只读句柄、可执行文件和当前目录不再算作写入，无关的、读不到的进程也不会让迁移无法开始。确实在写入时，提示会列出具体进程名和进程号；访问权限不足则单独提示去系统设置检查权限。刚启动、登记尚未完成的 AppPorts 辅助进程会在一秒内按进程号、启动时间和能力重新核对，而不是凭路径放行。

**运行中的关联应用先请求退出再继续** — 迁移或还原关联应用的数据时，不再只提示「请先关闭应用」，而是显示「退出应用并继续」：AppPorts 请求应用正常退出并最多等待 8 秒，仍未退出时提示你先完成保存，再点「继续」。

**迁移只搬数据，签名单独发起** — 数据迁移不再顺带修改关联应用的签名，也不会因为遗留偏好在你没有选择时重签。重签名和恢复原始签名仍然是应用内单独的、需要确认的操作，并会说明保留什么、临时占用多少空间。

**签名菜单跟随当前状态** — 已重签的应用保留「恢复原始签名」，不再显示重复重签入口；恢复官方状态后，才重新显示「重签名此应用」。

**应用列表即时反映操作结果** — 迁出、链接和还原成功后，两侧列表按服务返回的真实结果立即更新，不必等待整轮扫描，失败的项目不会显示成成功。手动刷新会强制重新测量大小，自动扫描继续复用有效缓存；还原已经生效但外部清理未完成时，外部副本行会保留。

**替换与覆盖前先核对** — 本地和外部同时存在同一应用且无法自动比较版本时，会先问你要保留哪个版本（「使用本地版本并继续」）；应用身份或版本在确认后发生变化时停止替换并请你重新选择，不会用不确定的对象覆盖。套件形式的本地入口如果包含个人文件或其他真实内容，AppPorts 会先请你把这些内容移到其他位置，再执行还原。

**数据操作后回收不再需要的签名备份** — 数据迁移、还原和挂载操作结束后，AppPorts 会检查该应用不再需要的签名备份并清理；清理不了时在「操作尚未完成」提示里说明，不会静默留下占用空间的文件。

### 文档与项目支持

- 文档站改用独立的 Fumadocs 站点，只维护简体中文、繁体中文和英文；三语各有 27 篇正文，统一导航、搜索和章节位置，包含使用步骤、原理、两篇实验博客、历史功能归档、隐私政策、开源许可和名词解释。其余语言与旧地址退出，不再提供跳转兼容。
- 迁移、签名和恢复的决策笔记集中到仓库内的 `.agents/notes/`，并新增阅读指南，方便后续维护者追溯每一处改动的原因。
- 「关于 AppPorts」的赞助名单加入 VC 与 zed，README 与仓库内置名单同步更新。

### 修复

- 针对企业微信迁移 `Data/tmp` 后启动崩溃的问题，禁止新迁移此类由 macOS 管理的容器结构，并保留旧迁移的还原入口。相关反馈：[#65](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/65)。
- 修复官方原包验签失败后仍继续重签、导致没有可恢复原包的问题；现在验签失败或超时会直接停止操作。
- 修复重签准备失败后，已撤回的操作仍可能被后台维护继续提交的问题。
- 修复中断续作已经完成重签后，又重复执行或因迟到的取消而被报告为失败的问题。
- 修复挂载或还原在确认本地目录可访问之前就卸载数据卷，导致原入口变成不可写空目录的问题；现在先确认本地目录可访问，失败时保留当前挂载。
- 修复 iOS 包装应用的本地入口把应用标识写成占位值、版本回退为 1.0 的问题；现在从内层应用读取标识，读不到时停止操作，而不是写入一个错误的入口。
- 修复系统标记（来源标记、按应用授权标记）变化被当作内容被修改，导致校验已经通过却无法清理旧副本的问题。
- 修复包含命名管道（部分数据库会用到）的目录无法迁移的问题；现在复制节点类型、权限和硬链接关系，但不读取管道中的瞬时消息，socket 仍然拒绝。
- 修复只读访问或无关的不可读进程被当作写入者、使操作无法开始的问题。
- 修复 AppPorts 更新或移动后，后台挂载任务因签名变化无法启动的问题。
- 修复点击状态统计只滚动到第一条匹配目录、其他状态仍混在列表里的问题。
- 修复容器的个人目录快捷方式被计入应用大小、并错误出现迁移入口的问题。
- 修复在不同窗口中修改自定义扫描目录或目录迁移配置后，其他窗口仍显示旧列表的问题。
- 修复启动和后台维护时，偏好变更通知从后台线程直接触发界面刷新的问题，保留多窗口扫描目录同步。
- 修复还原已经生效、但外部副本清理未完成时，外部副本行被隐藏、看起来像已彻底完成的问题。

### ⚠️ “AppPorts”已损坏，无法打开

如果从 AppPorts 官方发布渠道下载后遇到此提示，可能与 macOS 对未进行 Developer ID 签名和公证的应用进行隔离有关。

确认下载来源后，将 AppPorts 拖入「应用程序」文件夹，再在终端运行：

```shell
xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppPorts.app
```

### 迁移使用提示

- 经典数据迁移模式仍然默认关闭：它允许容器数据改用符号链接迁移，并允许对沙盒应用重签名，风险更高，需要逐次确认；保留原始签名的挂载迁移仍然是推荐方式，条件与步骤见 [挂载迁移说明](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/docs/datamigrae/baseinfo#mount)。
- 升级后建议检查三件事：目录页的挂载状态是否符合预期（已挂载 / 待挂载 / 外置盘未连接，连接外置盘后会自动接回）、设置是否提示旧登录任务清理失败（出现时点「重试」）、带「签名已替换」标记的应用是否还需要修复。
- 迁移后的目录请继续按原来的习惯使用：先连接外置盘，拔盘前先退出应用并正常推出，重要数据另行备份。

遇到问题或有新的建议，欢迎通过 [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues) 向我反馈。

## AppPorts v1.9.1 (build 32) Release Notes · [Download](https://file.shimoko.com/AppPorts)

### Summary

**Keep the apps and data you rely on, and give your Mac room for what comes next.** AppPorts 1.9.1 makes it easier to see which data you can move: the app-data list hides protected system structure by default while keeping eligible subdirectories visible. Click a status such as Linked or Mount migration to find the matching entries, with less digging through layers of folders.

Waiting for a large transfer should come with a clear view of what is happening. The new progress display explains preparation, copying, verification, and cleanup, showing the current work and how long it has been since the last progress. After an interruption, AppPorts uses its records to continue, restore the original entry, or finish the remaining cleanup; when it cannot confirm that proceeding is safe, it keeps the data and explains why. Existing migrations continue to follow their records after the update, without asking you to move everything again.

The space you reclaim should stay available to you. Official originals retained before re-signing now go automatically into a visible `AppPorts Backups` folder on an external drive, with a README for when you need to restore them. Migration moves data, and signing remains your separate choice. Older backups and copies are cleaned up once they are confirmed to be no longer needed, leaving your internal disk for your next project, your next video, and whatever you want to make next.

Everyday use gets easier too: the app list reflects operation results promptly, ordinary external apps can be excluded from duplicate Spotlight indexing, and the directory details panel remembers the height you choose. Thank you to everyone who shares a problem or a real use case. These improvements come from those experiences. I hope reclaiming space also leaves you with a little less to worry about.

### Upgrade Notes

**Open AppPorts once after updating.** This update retires the login-time re-signing task on every macOS version: the old script becomes a no-op first, then its processes are stopped and the login item is removed. The obsolete switch is removed; Settings offers a retry only if cleanup fails. From then on, signature work happens only as an explicit action inside the app.

**Upgrading asks you to redo nothing.** Directories you already migrated can stay where they are: everyday use, reconnecting after you plug the drive in, and restoring when you need to all follow the existing records, with no trip back to local storage and no second migration. This update also leaves app signatures alone, so an app you re-signed earlier does not need signing again because of the upgrade. The one exception is container data migrated with symbolic links in Classic Mode: if you want to restore its original signature, move that data back to local storage first. Directories migrated through an APFS mount are unaffected and can be repaired directly.

**Only apps whose signature AppPorts replaced need recovery.** Use Repair or Restore Original Signature on an app marked “Signature replaced”; recovery uses the official original saved before re-signing and needs no developer private key. Do not re-sign other apps “just in case.”

**Connect an external drive before re-signing an officially signed app.** Its original is saved externally even if the app itself stays on the internal disk. Without a writable external drive with enough space, the operation stops before changing the installed app. Apps on the internal disk still need temporary working space during the operation, and restoring requires the drive holding the original.

**When your external drive is disconnected, a directory shows “External drive not connected” and stays non-writable.** It reconnects automatically once the drive is back, or you can mount it from the row. Do not let an app create new data there before mounting completes, and keep a separate backup of important data.

Mount migration still requires an **unencrypted APFS external drive** and **Full Disk Access** for AppPorts. Move AppPorts into Applications first. Other storage formats remain usable for ordinary app and directory migrations.

### New Features

**Transfer progress reports the real work stages** — The operation window for built-in data directories and custom folders follows the actual stages: waiting for another operation, preparing, scanning source files, copying files, writing to disk, verifying files, switching the local entry, cleaning up old copies, and automatically recovering the data entry. Each stage carries a sentence explaining what is happening. A percentage belongs to file copying only, and says so—the copy is followed by verification and cleanup. Scanning, verification, and cleanup instead report items processed in this pass, bytes read, and the current file, alongside total and per-stage time.

**Clear wording when nothing new arrives for a while** — After 15 seconds without new file progress, the window reports how long it has been since the last progress instead of letting a timer imply work. Copy speed hides after 3 seconds without an update so a stale rate cannot mislead you. The window reports only known stages and real activity; it does not promise an estimated finish time.

**Exclude external apps from search** — A new toolbar entry on the Apps tab moves ordinary standalone apps into a dedicated app library on the external drive (`AppPorts.noindex`) so Spotlight no longer indexes both the local entry and the external app, which reduces duplicate search results. Your local entry keeps working, and Dock pins are pointed at the new location. App Store apps, iOS apps, and suite folders keep their original install paths and are left alone, and search for documents and photos on the drive is unaffected. The panel lists each app as Completed or Not completed before you click Process. Related report: [#67](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/67).

### Interface and Directory Browsing

**See which directories you can migrate right in the list** — The app-data list hides protected system structure by default while keeping eligible subdirectories visible, with the appropriate Migrate, Mount Migration, Restore, or other action on each row. A new Show Locked Directory Structure toggle sits beside Show Zero-byte Directories; turn it on to inspect those rows and hover over a lock icon to see why migration is unavailable. The toggle controls visibility only and does not remove system-directory protections. Existing migrations, recovery entries, and unreadable or conflicting paths remain visible.

**Status summaries now filter exactly** — Clicking a summary such as Linked, Mount migration, or Existing symlink shows only the matching rows while keeping the path context you need. The counts still reflect the full list before filtering, so you can switch to another state at any time; click again or clear the filter to restore everything, and changing app or tab resets the selection.

**Personal-folder links are no longer counted as app data** — Ordinary container shortcuts to Desktop, Downloads, Movies, Music, and Pictures are excluded from the app-data list. AppPorts does not traverse or measure their targets or offer migration or restoration, so personal files are not mistaken for data belonging exclusively to one app. Entries with existing managed records or requiring recovery or investigation remain visible.

**Clearer directory context and size scope** — Directories named `Data` keep their parent container path visible so you can tell them apart. Sizes state their scope (this volume or the link target), with an explanation that each row counts files independently, that a parent is not the sum of its children, and that logical size is not disk usage.

**The information panel remembers its height** — The directory information panel starts as a compact single-line path while keeping Copy Path and Show in Finder. The height you drag it to is remembered, including after you return to a larger window.

### Improvements

**Interrupted operations finish on their own** — After an interrupted migration, restore, or mount operation, AppPorts decides from the actual volume, the directory identity, and its durable records whether to continue, restore the original entry, or only finish the cleanup, so you no longer have to judge between copies. If the new location has already been written to, an old copy never overwrites it; when identity or content cannot be confirmed, the materials are kept, the reason is shown in the “operation not fully complete” notice, and Retry is offered.

**Retained originals no longer need a separate page** — Originals that pass verification are cleaned up automatically to free space, and those that cannot be proven safe are kept with an explanation. You are no longer asked to open a separate copy-management page and decide which copy belongs to whom.

**App-copy cleanup retries once on the original baseline** — After an app's location has switched, if a single cleanup observation fails because of a brief change, AppPorts re-checks immediately against the same verified baseline instead of reporting a pending task, so a cleanup that finishes in the background no longer leaves an outdated failure message. A persistent difference still keeps the old copy.

**Data volumes use system creation and explicit ownership-ignoring mounts** — Dedicated volumes for mount migration are created with the system's volume tooling and mounted with ownership checks off, so a normal user can write to them without changing ownership settings for the whole external drive. Older records without ownership information are interpreted the same way; historical operations with a strict ownership contract still follow their recorded contract.

**The local entry is checked before unmounting or restoring** — Before removing a mount or switching back to local data, AppPorts actually opens and reads the local directory and re-checks the transaction, target directory, and writers. If access is denied or a lease fails, the current mount is kept and you get Access Permission Settings and Retry, instead of unmounting first and discovering the local directory is unusable. The Restore action stays visible in all three mount states (mounted, pending mount, and external drive not connected), and an interrupted restore continues from that same entry.

**Older migrations can be restored directly** — Existing managed links keep their Restore action even when the directory is no longer eligible for a new migration under the current rules. Older links marked Needs Normalization can also be restored directly without first being moved to the current managed path. Related report: [#65](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/65).

**Long tasks are no longer cut off by a fixed overall limit** — The background mount task used to have one blanket force-exit deadline, which could end a large copy or verification halfway. There is no fixed limit for the whole operation now, while each disk command keeps its own deadline and error propagation; an interrupted run can still be retried from the normal entry. If you quit AppPorts while an operation is running, it cancels the operation and waits for it to unwind safely instead of ending the process in the middle of a write.

**The background mount task follows AppPorts updates** — Its definition now includes the current executable's signing identity, so a signature change after an update or move re-registers it, and a missing service is registered again. The task stays installed while a restore is pending and is removed only after the last restore and cleanup finish.

**Signature originals are saved automatically on an external drive** — AppPorts first uses the app’s external volume, then the existing external library’s volume, then another writable external drive with enough space. Originals go into a visible `AppPorts Backups` folder at the volume root with a `README.txt`; there is no new location picker or management page. The operation stops when no suitable drive is available. Retention on the same volume uses a rename; across volumes, the internal temporary original is removed only after the external copy is verified. Useful older internal originals move out automatically. Unrecoverable legacy records are removed only when their provenance is independently preserved or the official installation has been verified.

**Signature originals are kept and retired by recovery value** — The official original saved before re-signing is kept for as long as it has recovery value; it is retired only once the official state is proven (a verified update or reinstall from the same developer, with signature, data, and application-group dependencies checked). A changed signature hash never authorizes deletion by itself, and offline, damaged, unidentified, or unknown-origin originals are always kept. Re-signing the same version again never overwrites its first saved official original. Restoration runs from the saved original and needs no developer private key.

**One final full verification, with metadata checked by scope** — Copying no longer repeats per-file readback. After the tree is written and synchronized and every progress callback has finished, the destination is verified once for content, metadata, and structure, the source is checked again, and only then does the switch happen; the verification reuses a single full scan, which reduces repeated reads on large directories. Provenance markers and per-app access-grant markers are maintained by the system: they are not copied, not deleted, and a change in them is never treated as changed content, while application xattrs, ACLs, permissions, resource forks, and content are still checked as before.

**Only real writers block an operation** — Writer checks now look at how each file descriptor is opened: read-only handles, executables, and working directories no longer count as writes, and unrelated processes that cannot be inspected no longer prevent a transfer from starting. When something really is writing, the message names the process and its ID; insufficient access gets its own message pointing to System Settings. A just-started AppPorts helper whose registration has not finished is re-checked within a second by process ID, start time, and capability instead of being admitted by its path.

**A running related app is asked to quit before continuing** — Migrating or restoring an app's data no longer stops at “please close the app.” AppPorts offers Quit App and Continue, asks the app to quit normally, waits up to 8 seconds, and if it is still running asks you to finish saving and then click Continue.

**Migration moves data only; signing is a separate action** — Data migration no longer changes the related app's signature as a side effect, and no leftover preference can re-sign an app you did not choose. Re-signing and restoring the original signature remain explicit, confirmed actions in the app that state what is retained and how much temporary space is needed.

**Signing actions follow the current state** — A re-signed app keeps Restore Original Signature and hides the redundant re-sign action. Re-sign This App returns once the official state has been restored.

**The app list reflects results immediately** — After a move-out, link, or restore succeeds, both lists update immediately from the service's actual result instead of waiting for a full scan, and failed items are not shown as successful. A manual refresh forces sizes to be measured again while automatic scans reuse valid caches; when a restore has taken effect but external cleanup has not finished, the external copy row stays visible.

**Checks before replacing or overwriting** — When the same app exists locally and externally and the versions cannot be compared automatically, AppPorts first asks which version to keep (Use Local Version and Continue). If an app's identity or version changes after you confirm, the replacement stops and asks you to choose again rather than overwriting an uncertain object. If a suite-style local entry contains personal files or other real content, AppPorts asks you to move them elsewhere before restoring.

**Signature backups that are no longer needed are reclaimed** — After a data migration, restore, or mount operation, AppPorts checks whether the app's signature backups are still needed and cleans up the ones that are not. Anything it cannot clean is reported in the “operation not fully complete” notice instead of quietly taking up space.

### Documentation and Project Support

- The documentation site now runs independently on Fumadocs in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English. Each language has 27 articles with shared navigation, search, and chapter positions, covering practical steps, how migration works, two research blogs, historical features, privacy, licenses, and a glossary. Other languages and old routes are retired without compatibility redirects.
- Decision notes for migration, signing, and recovery are collected under `.agents/notes/` in the repository, with a new reading guide so future maintainers can trace why each change was made.
- VC and zed were added to the AppPorts sponsor list in About, with the README and the bundled repository list kept in sync.

### Fixes

- Moving WeCom's `Data/tmp` could cause a startup crash. AppPorts now blocks new migrations of such system-managed container structure and keeps Restore available for older managed migrations. Related report: [#65](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/65).
- Fixed re-signing continuing after verification of the official original failed, which could leave no restorable original. Verification failures and timeouts now stop the operation.
- Fixed background maintenance potentially committing a withdrawn signing operation after preparation had failed.
- Fixed recovery repeating an already completed re-sign or reporting it as failed when cancellation arrived after the change had taken effect.
- Fixed mount and restore operations unmounting a data volume before confirming the local directory was accessible, which could leave the original entry as an unwritable empty directory. AppPorts now confirms local access first and keeps the current mount if that check fails.
- Fixed the local entry for wrapped iOS apps writing a placeholder app identity and falling back to version 1.0. The identity is now read from the inner app, and the operation stops rather than writing an incorrect entry when it cannot be read.
- Fixed changes to system markers (provenance and per-app access grants) being treated as modified content, which blocked cleanup of old copies even though verification had passed.
- Fixed directories containing named pipes (used by some databases) failing to migrate. Node type, permissions, and hard-link relationships are now copied without reading transient messages from the pipe, while sockets are still refused.
- Fixed read-only or unrelated unreadable processes being treated as writers and preventing an operation from starting.
- Fixed the background mount task failing to start after AppPorts was updated or moved because its signature had changed.
- Fixed clicking a status summary only scrolling to the first matching directory while other states stayed mixed into the list.
- Fixed container shortcuts to personal folders being counted in app size and incorrectly offering a migration action.
- Fixed custom scan directories and directory-migration configurations changed in one window not appearing in another.
- Fixed preference changes during startup and background maintenance reaching the UI from a background thread, while preserving scan-directory synchronization across windows.
- Fixed the external copy row being hidden when a restore had taken effect but external cleanup had not finished, which made the restore look fully complete.

### ⚠️ “AppPorts” is damaged and can’t be opened

If this appears after downloading AppPorts from an official release channel, it may be related to macOS quarantine checks for apps without Developer ID signing and notarization.

After confirming the download source, move AppPorts to the Applications folder and run:

```shell
xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppPorts.app
```

### Migration Notes

- Classic Data Migration Mode remains off by default: it allows container data to use symbolic-link migration and allows re-signing sandboxed apps, which carries more risk and requires per-operation confirmation. Mount migration that preserves the original signature is still recommended; requirements and steps are in [Mount Migration](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/en/docs/datamigrae/baseinfo#mount).
- After upgrading, check three things: that the mount states on the Data Directories page match your expectation (Mounted / Pending Mount / External drive not connected, which reconnects automatically once the drive is back), whether Settings reports a failure to remove the old login task (click Retry if it does), and whether apps marked “Signature replaced” still need repair.
- Keep using migrated directories as before: connect the external drive first, quit the app and eject the drive normally before disconnecting it, and keep a separate backup of important data.

Share problems or suggestions through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues).
